title: Portuguese reach Timor
description: Portuguese traders exploring beyond Malacca reach the island and begin the trade in its sandalwood, later settling Dominican missionaries on its shores.

title: First governor of Portuguese Timor
description: António Coelho Guerreiro takes office at Lifau as the first governor of a Portuguese Timor now separate from the neighbouring islands.

title: Capital moved to Dili
description: The governor moves the capital from disease-ridden Lifau to Dili, which remains Timor's chief town.

title: Treaty of Lisbon
description: Portugal and the Netherlands divide Timor: the east plus the Oecusse enclave stay Portuguese and the west goes to the Dutch, a border that still stands.

title: Boaventura revolt crushed
description: Portuguese forces with African auxiliaries crush the revolt of Boaventura of Manufahi, the last great uprising against colonial rule.

title: Japanese invade Timor
description: Japan invades neutral Portuguese Timor to crush Australian and Dutch commandos; the occupation that follows kills a large share of the population.

title: Pro-independence parties form
description: After Portugal's Carnation Revolution ends censorship, Timorese form their first political parties, including the ASDT that soon becomes the pro-independence Fretilin.

title: Declaration of independence
description: Facing Indonesian attack after a brief civil war, Fretilin proclaims the Democratic Republic of East Timor, which Indonesia invades nine days later.

title: Indonesia annexes East Timor
description: Indonesia formally makes East Timor its 27th province, a step the United Nations never recognises.

title: Kraras massacre
description: Indonesian troops execute several hundred villagers at Kraras, one of the worst single massacres of the occupation.

title: Santa Cruz massacre
description: Indonesian troops fire on a funeral procession at the Santa Cruz cemetery, killing more than 250; smuggled-out footage turns world opinion against the occupation.

title: Xanana Gusmão captured
description: The leader of the armed resistance is captured in a Dili house and jailed in Jakarta, from where he continues to direct the movement.

title: Nobel Peace Prize
description: Bishop Carlos Belo and exiled diplomat José Ramos-Horta share the Nobel Peace Prize for their work towards a just end to the conflict.

title: INTERFET lands
description: After pro-Indonesian militias wreck the territory for voting to leave Indonesia, an Australian-led international force lands and restores order.

title: UN takes over
description: The Security Council sets up a transitional administration to govern East Timor until independence.

title: Independence restored
description: East Timor becomes independent as the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste with Xanana Gusmão as its first president, the first new state of the century.

title: 2006 crisis
description: A revolt by dismissed soldiers spirals into gang violence and army splits, forcing out prime minister Alkatiri and bringing foreign peacekeepers back.

title: Assassination attempts
description: Rebels shoot and nearly kill president Ramos-Horta and attack the prime minister's convoy; rebel leader Alfredo Reinado is killed at the president's house.

title: Taur Matan Ruak president
description: Former guerrilla commander Taur Matan Ruak is sworn in as president on the tenth anniversary of independence, and the UN mission closes at the year's end.
